<reflection>
The second experiment (higher catalyst) increased the spread of NLL values compared to the first run, but many mechanisms still cluster closely. M7 remains the best fit, but M16, M17, M14, M20, and M11 are within 0.65 NLL units, indicating they remain plausible. The large cluster around -43.45 (M2, M10, M1, M15, M9, M13, M19) shows these mechanisms are still competitive. The aim of stressing catalyst-dependent processes was partially achieved, but further discrimination is needed across the entire set.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Introducing initial product (0.2 M) while keeping substrate at 1.0 M and catalyst at 0.01 M will probe reversibility and product-sensitive pathways. Mechanisms with product inhibition (M12, M17), product-dependent deactivation (M12, M17), or reversible catalytic steps (present in most mechanisms) will respond differently to pre-existing product. This condition avoids repeating previous regimes and tests a new dimension: product concentration. It should help distinguish the top group (M7, M16, M17, etc.) from the large cluster and within the cluster, as mechanisms with product sensitivity will show altered kinetics compared to the product-free run at the same catalyst and substrate levels.
</hypothesis>
